caption: Jesus himself compares his fate with Moses’s raised bronze snake. It is powerful Christian typology—but Numbers tells a past rescue, not a forecast.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Is Jesus the raised bronze snake? Moses raises a bronze snake so bitten Israelites can look and live. Jesus says the Son of Man must be lifted up too.
slides.body: Moses raises a bronze snake so bitten Israelites can look and live. Jesus says the Son of Man must be lifted up too.
slides.heading: Is Jesus the raised bronze snake?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Num 21:9: Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole. If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live.
slides.body: Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole. If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live.
slides.heading: Num 21:9

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 3:14–15, BSB: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.
slides.body: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 3:14–15

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Jesus makes the connection John repeats “lifted up” and compares rescue from snakebite with eternal life through belief in Jesus.
slides.body: John repeats “lifted up” and compares rescue from snakebite with eternal life through belief in Jesus.
slides.heading: Jesus makes the connection

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Numbers tells a past rescue Numbers describes a wilderness emergency and cure. John later reads it as a pattern for Jesus’s death and exaltation.
slides.body: Numbers describes a wilderness emergency and cure. John later reads it as a pattern for Jesus’s death and exaltation.
slides.heading: Numbers tells a past rescue

title: The snake on the pole
